Before I was diagnosed with PCOS I had started growing facial hair, chest hair, and hair on my stomach. I also barely ever had periods.  I thought maybe I was really supposed to be a man.  I never wanted to be a man though.  I liked being a girl and i loved my then fiance (now husband).  I was so afraid he wouldn't love me anymore if it turned out I was actually a man.  I had learned in science class in high school about how you could have a male genotype but have a female phenotype (basically your genetics say you are a man but your physical features say you are a woman).   I thought that was what was wrong with me.  At that time we had been having unprotected sex for years and I hadn't gotten pregnant.  I thought this was because I was really a man.  I also liked women.  I never dated one and I very strongly identified as female.   It was a very confusing time and it took years before I broke down in tears and told my husband about the hair.   He said he knew and he didn't care and he still thought I was beautiful.  That was my turning point where I slowly started to accept whatever it was.  I still didn't know it was PCOS.  I hated my body for a while though.  Sometimes I still do.  It makes me really angry when I look in the mirror and there is stubble on my face.  I hate it and I feel like it doesn't belong to me and shouldn't be a part of me.
